scope: Present exposed remains of the Temple of Athena Polias in Priene. The five re-erected columns of the north peristasis, marble substructure, ruined cella and nearby fallen temple fragments.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Otto Bauer’s 1965–66 measurement records the four stylobate sides and the mostly surviving stepped platform.
The 2017 conservation study records the northern row, current height of 7.92 m, 1.29 m shaft diameter, 24 flutes, the missing torus, and steps of 0.36, 0.37 and 0.34 m.
Wolf Koenigs’s archaeological study identifies the 3.533 m center spacing that drove the plan grid.

limitations: The mapped 14.0 m ruin width is narrower than the surveyed 19.52 m stylobate. Greater width comes from the architectural measurement, with its center relative to mapped remnants approximate.

The exact five column centerpoints within the northern row, individual fragment positions, cellular wall remnants and modern visitor-ground details require interpretation. The southern temenos walls, altar and Propylon are outside the temple model.
The public elevation is preserved, but coarse source terrain cannot resolve individual stones or the original stepped paving.
next: Set the surviving stylobate datum and place the five re-erected north-side Ionic columns, battered stairs, low cella ruins and fallen white marble fragments.

sectionDatum.basis: Level at the top of the three stepped courses above the original northern grade.
